title: Rapid TTFT stabilizer: cross-deployment surge response and hedged prefetch rewrite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported sustained TTFT regressions and ~25-40% drop in tokens/sec for several long-context and INT8-quantized variants after a scheduled kernel-selection heuristic change. Scope: incidents impacted ~8% of production requests in US-west and EU regions, disproportionally affecting sessions with long priming sequences (>2k tokens) and bursty fanout patterns. Hypothesis: a tie-breaking change in the kernel selection path combined with the new continuous-batching window caused late-prefetch paths to lose hedging; KV cache prefetches were frequently deferred into the serving critical path, introducing first-byte stalls and lower token throughput. Objective: ship a safe hotfix that restores prefetch hedging, adds quantile-based router weight limits to prevent starvation, and stabilizes TTFT across Hosted/Dedicated/Private without a broad kernel rollback.
observed_metrics: First token latency (p50) regressed from 45ms -> 180ms for affected sessions
Tokens/sec per-worker dropped 35% on average for quantized int8 variants during peak fanout
Error rate: no increase in 5xxs; impact is performance-only but caused multiple customer escalations
Affected models: long-context Llama-variant-30k, Redwood-curated-open-compat-7B-INT8, mixed-attention experimental variants
steps_to_reproduce: Replay customer trace (trace id example: t-20250209-uhf3) with long priming (>2000 tokens) in canary region
Configure high fanout (3-5 model variants) and enable kernel-selection heuristic flag 'kern_sel_v2'
Run load profile from benchmark harness 'bench/priority-surges' with short inter-arrival times
Observe p50 first-token latency spike and queueing on prefetch worker threads
proposed_fix: Implement hedged-prefetch fastpath: when kernel-selection yields tie/low-confidence and request matches long-context/quantized profile, issue a parallel low-priority prefetch to dedicated prefetch worker pool and continue light-weight serving path. Add quantile-based router weight caps to prevent any single variant from taking >40% effective prefetch bandwidth during bursts. Add telemetry: prefetch latency histogram and prefetch-cancel rate to console. Ship as a staged rollout: canary (5% traffic) -> region rollouts -> global. No config change required from customers.
rollout_plan: Patch runtime and router in branch fix/hedged-prefetch-ENG-875999
Deploy canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic and dashboards monitored: prefetch latency, first-token p50/p95, tokens/sec worker
Hold for 4 hours of steady metrics and two customer confirmations from impacted accounts in canary region
Progressively expand 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 24 hours unless regressions observed
If regression at any stage: instant rollback using runtime feature-flag and route traffic to previous kernel-selection path
test_plan: Unit tests for hedged-prefetch state machine and cancelation logic
Integration test in staging with long-context fixtures and quantized models
Load test reproducing token surge profile (bench/priority-surges) and assert tokens/sec >= baseline-90%
Customer-acceptance: deploy canary to one affected customer's dedicated cluster with opt-in telemetry
acceptance_criteria: First-token p50 for affected sessions returns to <=1.2x baseline within canary period
Tokens/sec drop limited to <=10% vs baseline under the same load profile
No increase in 5xx or memory OOM incidents during canary
Telemetry added to Console with alert thresholds and runbook linked

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hedged prefetch increases background bandwidth and may raise cost on very high-fanout customers. Mitigation: cap hedged-prefetch per-tenant and add router weight limits (default 40%).
Risk: Backport for Private (air-gapped) could require manual bundle and testing matrix. Mitigation: create a minimal patch bundle and run the customer's provided smoke scripts before release.
Risk: Edge cases with prefetch cancellation may leak tasks. Mitigation: add timeout and GC checks, and run leak detection during canary
